meta.unit: The signs and the robber wars (3 Nephi 1–7)
principles: Peace with nothing left to hinder it
Ranks formed out of riches and schooling
A law broken by the men who administer it

world_behind.title: They stayed gathered four years after the war ended
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 5:6 and 7 have the combinations put down and the twenty-second through twenty-fifth years pass away. Verses 1 and 2 have the people return to their own lands only in the twenty-sixth, so the defensive concentration of 3 Nephi 3:22 to 25 was held for four years after the danger was gone.

world_behind.title: The ex-robbers are given land
world_behind.text: Verse 3 grants ground to those who covenanted to keep the peace and desired to remain Lamanites. 3 Nephi 5:4 had already preached to the prisoners and freed those who covenanted, so this is the second stage of one settlement.

world_behind.title: The peace has named authors, and the office stays in a family
world_behind.text: Verse 6 credits Gidgiddoni, Lachoneus, and the leaders the people had appointed. Verse 19 then has Lachoneus the son of Lachoneus filling his father's seat inside the same decade.

world_behind.title: These are the roads the earthquake breaks
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 8 report many cities built anew, many old ones repaired, and highways and roads laid between them. 3 Nephi 8:13 has those same highways broken up and the level roads spoiled four years later.

world_behind.title: The signature law is a safeguard from Mosiah's reform
world_behind.text: Verses 22 to 24 say no lawyer, judge or high priest could condemn anyone to death without the governor's signature. Mosiah 29:25 to 29 built the system of judges and the higher judges who check them; this chapter reports that check being routed around by secrecy rather than repealed.

world_behind.title: The sequence repeats two centuries later
world_behind.text: Verses 10 to 14 run riches, then ranks, then pride, then the church broken up. 4 Nephi 1:24 to 26 gives the same order after the two hundredth year: costly apparel, goods no longer held in common, division into classes, churches built up to get gain.

words.text: Eaten up entirely. The record uses the word five times and the King James Bible fifty-three. Verse 2 uses it of stores that outlasted a four-year war.
Traders. It appears once in the record, and twenty-nine times in the King James Bible. Verse 11 lists merchants, lawyers, and officers together as the new occupations.
Grades of social standing. Treated at Mosiah 10:9, where it means rows of an army. The record uses the word twice, and the two senses are different.
Abusive speech. All three of the record's uses are in this one verse, and the King James Bible has it four times, including 1 Peter 3:9. Verse 13 has some returning it and others refusing to.
Unevenness of condition. Treated at Alma 16:16, where the Lord's word went out with no inequality among the people. The record uses the word six times and the King James Bible never.
Relatives, extended family. The word turns up twenty times here, and the King James Bible eight. Verse 27 has the accused judges' kindreds joining the lawyers and high priests.

phrases.term: They granted unto those robbers who had entered into a covenant... lands, according to their numbers
phrases.text: Land given to former enemies who kept an oath. Verse 3 adds that they wished to remain Lamanites, and the grant does not require otherwise.

phrases.term: There was nothing in all the land to hinder the people from prospering continually, except they should fall into transgression
phrases.text: Mormon naming the only remaining risk. The sentence is written by a man who knows which way it went.

phrases.term: Many highways cast up, and many roads made
phrases.text: Public works as the mark of the peace. Roads linking every city and every land are what four verses of prosperity produce.

phrases.term: There were many merchants in the land, and also many lawyers, and many officers
phrases.text: The three occupations Mormon names as the disputing begins. Alma 10:27 had put lawyers and judges at the foundation of an earlier collapse.

phrases.term: Distinguished by ranks, according to their riches and their chances for learning
phrases.text: The mechanism of the division, given in one clause. Money and access to schooling sort the people, and verse 12 notes that poverty produced the ignorance.

phrases.term: Some did return railing for railing
phrases.text: The verse divides the people by their response to abuse. The others took persecution and stayed humble and penitent.

phrases.term: There became a great inequality in all the land, insomuch that the church began to be broken up
phrases.text: Mormon's causal claim, stated as a sequence. The inequality of verse 12 is what the church could not survive.

phrases.term: They did not sin ignorantly, for they knew the will of God
phrases.text: The record closing off an excuse. They had been told, so the rebellion is called willful.

phrases.term: Those who were angry were chiefly the chief judges, and they who had been high priests and lawyers
phrases.text: The opposition identified by profession. Verse 21 adds that all the lawyers were angry.

phrases.term: Put to death secretly by the judges
phrases.text: The crime stated plainly. The secrecy exists because verse 22 required the governor's signature.

phrases.term: They did set at defiance the law and the rights of their country
phrases.text: The end of the chapter and of the republic. The covenant is to destroy the governor and establish a king.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: A logistical detail that closes an earlier plan
verses.text: The record follows the returning people with an accounting note: "they had not eaten up all their provisions; therefore they did take with them all that they had not devoured, of all their grain of every kind, and their gold, and their silver, and all their precious things." Seven years of stores were laid in at 3 Ne. 4:4 for a siege, and this verse reports the surplus. The whole strategy of gathering into one place is settled here not with a comment on its wisdom but with an inventory of what was left over.

verses.label: v. 7–8
verses.title: Public works, with two kinds of road distinguished
verses.text: The record describes the peace by what got built: "there were many cities built anew, and there were many old cities repaired." Verse 8 separates two categories that a summary would merge: "many highways cast up, and many roads made, which led from city to city, and from land to land, and from place to place." Cast up is a construction term for a raised roadbed, and it is applied only to the highways. The roads are simply made.

verses.label: v. 10–12
verses.title: Inequality described by its two axes
verses.text: The record names the professions that appeared, "many merchants in the land, and also many lawyers, and many officers," and then states the sorting principle outright: "the people began to be distinguished by ranks, according to their riches and their chances for learning." Two variables, money and education, and the phrase chances for makes the second a matter of access rather than of capacity. Verse 12 finishes the sentence with the consequences, "some were ignorant because of their poverty, and others did receive great learning because of their riches."

verses.label: v. 13
verses.title: A society described by pairs of opposites
verses.text: Rather than characterising the people as a whole, the record sets four contrasts side by side: "Some were lifted up in pride, and others were exceedingly humble; some did return railing for railing, while others would receive railing and persecution and all manner of afflictions, and would not turn and revile again." Both halves of each pair are reported as present at the same time. The verse gives no proportion and names no group, so what it establishes is that the division ran through the population rather than between two parties.

verses.label: v. 18
verses.title: An excuse ruled out before anyone offers it
verses.text: The record forecloses the obvious defence at once: "they did not sin ignorantly, for they knew the will of God concerning them, for it had been taught unto them; therefore they did wilfully rebel against God." The clause for it had been taught unto them supplies the evidence for the claim about their knowledge, and the therefore draws the conclusion. Nothing in the surrounding narrative requires the argument. The record makes it anyway, and it is about a state of mind rather than an act.

verses.label: v. 27–30
verses.title: A conspiracy identified by profession and by pedigree
verses.text: The record says who joined and it is a list of offices: "those judges had many friends and kindreds; and the remainder, yea, even almost all the lawyers and the high priests, did gather themselves together." Then it identifies the instrument they used by its history rather than its content: "they did enter into a covenant one with another, yea, even into that covenant which was given by them of old, which covenant was given and administered by the devil." Verse 30 states the object plainly, "they did covenant one with another to destroy the governor, and to establish a king over the land."

chapter.title: The peace is real and its authors are named
chapter.text: Verse 6 credits specific men. Mormon does not treat the good years as accidental.

chapter.title: Nothing external threatened them
chapter.text: Verse 5 says only transgression could stop the prospering. The chapter then spends twenty-five verses on transgression.

chapter.title: The division runs on money and schooling
chapter.text: Verse 12 names riches and chances for learning as what sorted the people, and identifies poverty as the cause of the ignorance.

chapter.title: Inequality is given as the cause of the break
chapter.text: Verse 14 puts it in a lone clause. The church is not persecuted apart; it comes apart along the seam described two verses earlier.

chapter.title: A remnant holds and is identified
chapter.text: The few converted Lamanites are called firm, steadfast, and immovable. They are the same people 3 Nephi 2:16 had numbered among the Nephites.

chapter.title: Ignorance is ruled out
chapter.text: Verse 18 says they knew and rebelled anyway. The record removes the mildest available explanation.

chapter.title: The killings are secret because the law worked
chapter.text: Verse 22 describes a real check requiring the governor's signature, and verse 23 describes men working around it.

chapter.title: The trial produces the conspiracy
chapter.text: Verses 26 through 30 have the prosecution of a few judges turn into a covenant to end the republic. 3 Nephi 7 opens with the governor dead.

applications.title: Give land to the people who kept their word
applications.text: Former enemies who covenanted were settled and left as themselves. Terms honored after the fighting are what make an ending stick.

applications.title: Name the only thing that can stop you
applications.text: The verse says there was nothing in all the land to hinder them from prospering, except that they should fall into transgression. Once the external obstacles clear, the whole remaining risk is internal, and that is the one nobody schedules a review for.

applications.title: Build the roads between
applications.text: After the war they cast up many highways and made roads from city to city and land to land. Recovery is more than repairing what was damaged; the connections between the pieces have to be built as well.

applications.title: Watch the seam, not the roof
applications.text: The church broke along a division that had formed in the economy first. Look for where a community is already sorted before asking why it split.

applications.title: Decide in advance about railing
applications.text: The verse divides people by whether they returned it. That is a policy you can set before the provocation arrives.

applications.title: Separate ignorance from will
applications.text: Mormon writes that they did not sin ignorantly, because the will of God had been taught them. Which of the two you are dealing with decides whether the answer is more teaching or something else entirely.

applications.title: Notice who gets angry at the criticism
applications.text: The chief judges, priests, and lawyers. When correction lands, the professions that object tell you where it landed.

applications.title: Check what makes a safeguard actually report
applications.text: No one could be put to death without the governor's signature, so the judges killed the prophets secretly and let the news arrive afterward. A rule that depends on people reporting themselves is only as good as whatever compels the report.

questions.text: What is the one thing that could actually derail my life right now?
What am I building that will outlast the season that allowed it?
Which rank am I in, and what put me there?
When was I last railed at, and what did I return?
What inequality am I part of and comfortable with?
What do I know the will of God about and not do?
What have I done quietly that I would not sign my name to?
